{{Short description|Hungarian-American mathematician (born 1924)}}
'''László Fuchs''' (born June 24, 1924) is a [[Hungary|Hungarian]]-born American mathematician, the Evelyn and John G. Phillips Distinguished Professor Emeritus in Mathematics at [[Tulane University]].<ref name="tu">[http://www.math.tulane.edu/faculty/fuchs.html Faculty profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110207164016/http://www.math.tulane.edu/faculty/fuchs.html |date=2011-02-07 }}, Tulane Univ., retrieved 2012-02-19.</ref> He is known for his research and textbooks in [[group theory]] and [[abstract algebra]].<ref name="goebel">{{citation
 | last = Göbel | first = Rüdiger
 | doi = 10.1007/BF01879728
 | issue = 1–2
 | journal = Periodica Mathematica Hungarica. Journal of the János Bolyai Mathematical Society
 | mr = 1407905
 | pages = 13–29
 | title = László Fuchs—a personal evaluation of his contributions to mathematics
 | volume = 32
 | year = 1996| s2cid = 119541716
 }}.</ref><ref name="moddom">{{citation
 | last = Salce | first = Luigi
 | contribution = László Fuchs and his “moddom” work
 | location = Providence, RI
 | mr = 1817146
 | pages = 3–7
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | series = Contemporary Mathematics
 | title = Abelian Groups, Rings and Modules (Perth, 2000)
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=FmbO7ia9VgoC&pg=PA3
 | volume = 273
 | year = 2001| isbn = 9780821856093
 }}.</ref>
[[File:Laszlo_fuchs.jpg|thumb|Fuchs in 1975]]

==Biography==
Fuchs was born on June 24, 1924, in [[Budapest]],<ref name="f70"/> into an academic family: his father was a linguist and a member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="f70"/> He earned a bachelor's degree in 1946 and a doctorate in 1947 from [[Eötvös Loránd University]].<ref name="f70"/><ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=37269}}</ref> After teaching high school mathematics for two years, and then holding positions at Eötvös Loránd, the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics|Mathematical Research Institute of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences]], and the [[University of Miami]], he joined the Tulane faculty in 1968.<ref name="f70"/><ref name="tu"/> At Tulane, Fuchs chaired the mathematics department from 1977 to 1979.<ref name="f70"/> He retired in 2004.<ref>[http://www.math.tulane.edu/newsletter/archive/newsletter/index.html Letter from Morris Kalka, Chair] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081228001513/http://www.math.tulane.edu/newsletter/archive/newsletter/index.html |date=2008-12-28 }}, Tulane Math Newsletter, January 2005, retrieved 2012-02-19.</ref>

In 2004, Fuchs was honored at the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] 80th anniversary as one of the "big five" most distinguished Hungarian mathematicians. The other honorees were [[John Horvath (mathematician)|John Horvath]], [[János Aczél (mathematician)|János Aczél]], [[Ákos Császár]] and [[Steven Gaal]].<ref name=big5>[http://netrix.mta.nsd.sztaki.hu/mta_hirei/fohajtas-ot-kiemelkedo-magyar-matematikus-teljesitmenye-elott-a-magyar-tudomanyos-akademian-134639/ Tribute to the achievements of five outstanding Hungarian mathematicians] Department of Mathematical Sciences of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences</ref> Fuchs has nearly 100 [[Academic genealogy|academic descendants]], many of them through his student at Eötvös Loránd, [[George Grätzer]].<ref name="mg"/> He was treasurer of the [[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]] from 1949 until 1963, and secretary-general of the society from 1963 to 1966.<ref name="f70"/>

Fuchs [[Centenarian|turned 100]] on June 24, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mta.hu/english/big-five-100-video-of-the-international-conference-celebrating-the-100th-anniversary-of-the-birth-of-five-legendary-mathematicians-113767|title=Big Five 100 – Video of the international conference celebrating the 100th anniversary of the birth of five legendary mathematicians|publisher=Hungarian Academy of Sciences|date=June 17, 2024|accessdate=June 30, 2024}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Fuchs won the [[Kossuth Prize]] in 1953.<ref name="f70"/> He is a foreign member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="f70">{{citation
 | doi = 10.1007/BF01879727
 | issue = 1–2
 | journal = Periodica Mathematica Hungarica. Journal of the János Bolyai Mathematical Society
 | mr = 1407904
 | pages = 1–12
 | title = László Fuchs' 70th birthday
 | volume = 32
 | year = 1996| s2cid = 189834633
 }}.</ref>
Two conferences were dedicated to him on the occasion of his 70th birthday, and another on his 75th.<ref name="f70"/><ref name="goebel"/><ref name="moddom"/>

At Tulane University, Fuchs held the W. R. Irby Professorship from 1979 to 1992, and the Evelyn and John G. Phillips Distinguished Professorship from then until his retirement.<ref name="f70"/>

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-12-29.</ref>
